questions.stem: Which of the following is the core component of an Operating System that manages system resources?
questions.explanation: The kernel is the central, core component of an Operating System that manages memory, processes, and hardware device communication.

questions.stem: Which command in Linux is used to list directory contents?
questions.explanation: The 'ls' command lists all files and folders in the current working directory in Linux.

questions.stem: What is the default file system used by modern Windows operating systems?
questions.explanation: NTFS (New Technology File System) is the default file system used by Windows NT and its successors (including Windows 10/11).

questions.stem: In Linux, what is the superuser account name?
questions.explanation: The 'root' account is the default administrative superuser account in Linux/Unix environments with full system privileges.

questions.stem: Which Windows tool allows users to view and manage active processes and system performance?
questions.explanation: Task Manager is the built-in utility in Windows that displays active processes, memory usage, CPU load, and network performance.

questions.stem: Which command is used in Linux to change file permissions?
questions.explanation: The 'chmod' (change mode) command modifies read, write, and execute permissions of files and directories in Linux.

questions.stem: What is the directory path of the system configuration files in Linux?
questions.explanation: The '/etc' directory in Linux hosts all system-wide configurations and initialization scripts.

questions.stem: What is the command-line shell interface for Windows called?
questions.explanation: PowerShell is the modern task automation and configuration management framework from Microsoft containing a command-line shell.

questions.stem: In Linux, which command is used to display the current directory path?
questions.explanation: The 'pwd' (print working directory) command prints the absolute path of the current working directory in the terminal.

questions.stem: Which Windows Registry hive contains configuration information specific to the currently logged-in user?
questions.explanation: HKEY_CURRENT_USER (HKCU) stores configuration profiles and settings for the user currently logged into the system.
